compute.cost_note: Standard-library rendering with in-repo helpers, no model, API or fresh scoring. No optional runtime dependencies are required. Reads the complete JSON and constructs window/signal grids in memory. Upstream measurement costs and heuristic caveats remain separate; Explicit files need a resolved ai-prose-baselines-private path component unless opted out. This path convention does not check permissions; stdout is not guarded. Paths and localization output can be sensitive without prose.

do_not_use_when: Input is raw manuscript prose or a non-windowed audit; this renderer requires a windows block.
You need a fresh score, baseline comparison or full upstream schema/provenance validation.
You want calibrated per-zone certainty, an authorship or AI verdict, or automatic scene-defect decisions.
Upstream register or baseline caveats make the window measurements inappropriate; rendering does not resolve those caveats.

examples.description: Render existing window measurements to explicitly private Markdown and JSON paths; routing registers inherit upstream applicability, not new calibration.

optional: --json-out caller-named schema 1.0 sidecar path; there is no --json flag.
--allow-public-output explicitly bypasses the private-root output-path convention for already-public material; it is not required for ordinary private output.
required: Existing sliding-window measurements as a raw windows block, legacy top-level windows, or current results.windows envelope; this is not full upstream schema/provenance validation.
inputs.target: variance_audit sliding-window JSON via stdin or --in (not manuscript prose).

artifacts: Optional caller-named Markdown file (for example heatmap.md); Markdown stdout is the default.
Optional caller-named JSON sidecar (for example heatmap.json); target.path identifies the input JSON path ('-' for stdin) and target.words is zero, not the manuscript count.

purpose: Render already-measured variance_audit window bands and flagged signals as a Markdown localization heatmap with an optional JSON sidecar. Heuristic operator cues for further investigation, not calibrated per-zone judgments.
use_when: You have sliding-window variance diagnostics and want to inspect word-coordinate hot zones, dominant signals and phenomenon cues.
You want to visualize existing measurements without running fresh scoring or loading a model.
